profiles.meeting_scenario: Chameleon’s research and platform workstreams are coordinating a handoff for an upcoming SME pilot with a mid-sized retail customer that wants a demand-forecasting model integrated into its weekly replenishment workflow. The meeting happens after the research team has finished a promising experiment branch using Chameleon’s model-and-loss zoo, while the platform side is preparing the templated deployment path and governance checks for a pilot-ready package. The agenda is to align on what artifact will be handed off this week, which shared dataset snapshot and template branch the teams are referring to, what 'ready' means for the pilot handoff, and how the testing framework results will be attached. The expected outcome is a seemingly straightforward agreement that Lena will deliver the 'production-ready template package' by Thursday and Omar will wire it into the standard Chameleon deployment path for the retail pilot.

members.name: Dr. Lena Vogt
members.expertise: robust modeling on real-world tabular data, loss-function design, experiment evaluation
members.background: Lena leads the Chameleon model-and-loss zoo workstream and has spent the last six months adapting demand-forecasting recipes for noisy SME retail data, with a strong focus on getting reliable offline performance quickly.
members.private_state: She wants the pilot handoff to happen without reopening modeling work, is proud that the latest run finally stabilized on sparse store histories, and worries that platform requirements could delay the external pilot if they trigger a broader packaging effort.
hidden_assumptions: When the team says a model is 'production-ready' in Chameleon, it means the model artifact, training config, and evaluation summary are stable enough for a customer pilot, even if service wrapping is still routine downstream work.

The 'retail pilot dataset' refers to the June frozen extract with the relabeled return transactions because that is the dataset used in her final experiments and the one mentioned in the latest research notes.

If the testing framework 'passes,' the meaningful bar is that the key failure-mode checks were run on the candidate model and manually inspected, not that every deployment automation check has already succeeded.
Sharing the 'template' means handing over the training recipe files and defaults that define the experiment, since inference packaging is owned by platform and follows standard conventions anyway.

members.name: Omar Haddad
members.expertise: ML infrastructure, deployment templating, CI/CD for model services, governance tooling
members.background: Omar maintains Chameleon’s templatable framework, deployment scaffolds, and automated test harnesses, and he specializes in turning research outputs into repeatable services for SME environments with minimal custom ops overhead.
members.private_state: He wants to keep the pilot onboarding low-touch by using the standard deployment template unchanged, and he is concerned that anything not already encoded in the scaffold will create manual work and brittle support obligations later.
hidden_assumptions: In a coordination context, 'production-ready' means the artifact is already in the standard service/package shape with manifests, inference hooks, and monitoring stubs so platform can deploy rather than reinterpret research outputs.

The 'retail pilot dataset' is the shared snapshot currently mounted in the platform staging bucket under the retail pilot name, because coordination usually references the canonical shared storage version unless someone explicitly says otherwise.

If someone says the testing framework is 'green' or that checks 'passed,' that implies the automated CI suite for the template package succeeded, since manual notebook review is research validation rather than release readiness.
When a researcher says they will send the 'template,' it means the full Chameleon template branch or package contents needed to instantiate a deployable project, not just experiment configs.
Unless stated otherwise, the current standard template means the latest mainline scaffold branch that already includes the new feature-contract generator.
